newsitem.title: USA: US governors oppose mandated electric competition.
newsitem.headline: US governors oppose mandated electric competition.

text.p: U.S. Midwest governors passed a resolution Monday opposing federally mandated competition in the retail electric industry.
The governors announced the decision at a news conference that concluded the annual meeting of the Midwestern Governor's Conference.
The governors said Congress and President Clinton should recognize that certain policies such as retail choice and cost discovery are best decided at the state and local levels.
The two-day conference, hosted by Kansas Gov. Bill Graves, featured discussions on deregulating the electric and telecommunications industries.

Kansas and other states are studying proposals to deregulate the electric industry through a system called retail wheeling, in which consumers would choose their electric company in much the same way as they now choose a long-distance telephone carrier.
The Midwestern Governors' Conference is made up of the governors of Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota and Wisconsin.
